title: Default omitted `workspace` arg to the stdio session's CWD workspace
description:
Every MCP tool required an explicit `workspace`; agents routinely omit it and have to recall. On the stdio path the server process shares the client session's CWD, so its containing workspace is a natural default.

Behavior: omit `workspace` → resolves to the workspace containing the stdio process's CWD; pass one → it wins unchanged; no default available (CWD outside any registered workspace, or the http daemon) → clear INVALID_PARAMS error, never a silent guess. Scope is stdio-only by design; the http daemon stays explicit-workspace-only since it serves many repos and has no single "current" workspace.

decisions.decision: Keep `workspace` as `String` with `#[serde(default)]` (empty = use default) rather than `Option<String>`
decisions.rationale: schemars still drops a serde-defaulted field from `required` so clients may omit it, while the String type keeps all 35 `&args.workspace` call sites compiling unchanged. Option<String> would force ~70 edits and a tool_context signature change.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Change field to Option<String> across 28 structs + 35 call sites

decisions.decision: Set the default only on the stdio path; http daemon stays explicit-workspace-only
decisions.rationale: The daemon serves many repos from one process and current_dir() is the daemon's launch dir, not the caller's — a CWD default there would silently answer from the wrong repo. Leaving default_workspace=None makes the daemon degrade to a clear error.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Compute the default inside SutraServer::new so both transports inherit it

implementation_plan:
- src/mcp.rs: `default_workspace: Option<String>` field + `with_default_workspace()` builder (threaded through new/clone). `resolve_workspace` substitutes the default for an empty arg — single chokepoint for tool_context/get_db/hold_parse_lock. New `canonical_ws_id()`; route await_parse + get_dd_engine through it so they key the parse lock / DD-engine map on the canonical id. `freshness()` echoes resolved `workspace` in every response.
- src/main.rs: `detect_cwd_workspace()` shared helper with longest-prefix match; maybe_reparse_cwd refactored onto it; default set only on the stdio path.
- 28 tool arg structs: `#[serde(default)]` on `workspace: String` (kept as String, empty = use default) so schemars drops it from `required` and all `&args.workspace` call sites compile unchanged.
execution_record:
Went as planned. Chose `#[serde(default)] workspace: String` (empty = default) over `Option<String>` to avoid ~70 edits (field type + every call site); keeps type String so handlers are untouched. Verification: 2 new tests in src/tools/grep.rs assert schemars drops workspace from `required` and serde tolerates omission; full suite 1564 passed / 3 ignored; clippy clean in touched files (9 pre-existing warnings elsewhere). Committed on main, not pushed.

Incidental fixes surfaced: (1) maybe_reparse_cwd used first-match `.find()` on CWD prefix — replaced with longest-prefix so a nested workspace beats an ancestor. (2) await_parse/get_dd_engine keyed a lock/hashmap on the raw arg string, desyncing from hold_parse_lock's canonical id when a path/basename (or now empty) was passed — routing through canonical_ws_id fixes both the new empty case and the pre-existing inconsistency.
